subject: Vela Commerce launch capacity multipliers & routing deconflict
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@velacorp.com>, Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@velacorp.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Vela Commerce beta launch — initial capacity signal and ask

Hi Sam / Elaine —

Thanks again for the details on the Vela beta. Per our run-through yesterday you indicated a heavy short-duration peak on day-of-launch plus sustained baseline traffic. To make the internal coordination straightforward I'm attaching our initial forecast (vela_launch_forecast_v1.csv) and a short summary below.

High-level ask: can we provision a temporary rate/quota uplift for the 72-hour launch window and set up a prioritized routing policy for the critical endpoints that handle checkout flows?

Forecast snapshot (from Vela):
- Expected baseline qps: ~60 RPS (mostly embeddings + small-gen calls)
- Peak burst qps: 950 RPS (10-15 minute spikes around promo events)
- Peak sustained window: 3 hours on day 0 at ~400 RPS
- Percent of calls that require generation with long seqs (>1024 tokens): ~12%

What we need from Redwood:
- Temporary per-customer quota multiplier (x8) during the 72-hour launch window
- Route critical endpoints to dedicated capacity or give them throttle exemption to avoid tail latency impact
- Monitoring and an on-call escalation plan

Can the product/infra teams confirm feasibility and an estimated lead time? We'd like to lock decisions by 2027-04-27 EOD to meet Vela's launch schedule.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: vela_launch_forecast_v1.csv (CSV)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@velacorp.com>, Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@velacorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vela Commerce beta launch — initial capacity signal and ask

Thanks Karthik — looping in product + infra to scope technical options. Quick clarifying questions for the forecast so engineering can size correctly: 

1) Are the 950 RPS spikes single instant bursts (seconds) or sustained 10–15 minute windows?
2) Can Vela provide a split of endpoint types (embeddings vs chat/generation) by % for peak traffic?
3) Do they expect a schema change / increased response size during promos

If we get those answers I can prioritize a short routing plan and cost estimate. Also confirming we'll need a signed throttle-exemption approval from the ops lead before we flip anything.

— Soojin
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@velacorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@velacorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vela Commerce beta launch — initial capacity signal and ask

Hi team — answers below and attaching a short readme (vela_profile_readme.pdf) with endpoint breakdowns.

1) Spikes: the 950 RPS are short bursts tied to flash promos — typically 8–12 minutes, sometimes repeated 2–3 times in an hour.
2) Endpoint mix (peak): 68% embeddings (user/product matching), 20% short-gen (templated responses <300 tokens), 12% long-gen (>1024 tokens).
3) No schema changes expected during launch; response sizes for embeddings are stable but generation calls may increase by ~10% tokens during promos.

We want to avoid 429s at all costs during promotions. If you can route checkout and payment validation endpoints to a higher priority we will accept the associated uplift charges; the commercial team is OK with a short-term premium.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Taylor
Head of Platform
Vela Commerce

[Attachment: vela_profile_readme.pdf (PDF)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@velacorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vela Commerce beta launch — product routing and options

Thanks for the details. Based on the breakdown there are two practical options we can offer Vela for the launch window:

Option A — Temporary quota multiplier + normal routing (fastest to enable)
- Apply x8 quota multiplier at the account level for 72 hours
- Pros: minimal infra changes; quick turn-on
- Cons: potential increased queueing and tail latency for heavy-gen calls

Option B — Priority routing + selective dedicated capacity (recommended)
- Route checkout/payment endpoints to a dedicated duty pool (reserved capacity) for the 72-hour window; keep other traffic on hosted pool
- Pros: isolates critical flows, reduces chance of user-visible errors
- Cons: requires pre-provisioning dedicated slots and a brief config rollout; ~24–36 hour lead time

For either option we'll need the following from Vela:
- Final list of critical endpoints (exact paths)
- Confirmed launch window start time (UTC) and any blackout windows

If infra approves we can prepare a rollback plan and set the monitoring thresholds to auto-fallback to regular routing if error rate > 2% for 10 minutes. Attached a proposed route_plan.md with the failover steps.

Evelyn
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: route_plan.md (MD)]

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@velacorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vela Commerce beta launch — infra feasibility + estimates

We can support Option B (priority routing + dedicated pool) but need the following to proceed:

- Final endpoint list and traffic weights at least 24 hours before provisioning
- Approval on provisional cost estimate (see capacity_estimates.xlsx) — rough estimate: $2.4k/day for the reserved pool during the window (depends on GPU sku).
- We will create a temporary runbook and a Slack incident channel; need one ops approver to be on-call during the window.

Operational notes:
- Provisioning lead time: 24 hours after sign-off for the dedicated pool (can be accelerated to ~12 hours with an engineer on standby but cost increases)
- Monitoring: we'll set SLO alerts for 95th/99th latency and error rates; automatic fallback if errors exceed threshold

If product signs off on exact endpoints, we can schedule the provisioning and add the route config to the rollout plan.

— Dylan
Infra / SRE
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: capacity_estimates.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@velacorp.com>, Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@velacorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-26T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vela Commerce beta launch — capacity multipliers & routing deconflict (APPROVAL)

All — thanks for the quick turn. Per the notes above and Vela confirmation, I'm approving Option B (priority routing + dedicated pool) for the 72-hour launch window starting 2027-05-01T15:00:00Z. Approvals/conditions: 

- Vela to provide exact endpoint list and final launch time by 2027-04-27T17:00:00Z
- Karthik to confirm commercial uplift acceptance in writing (ticket to finance)
- Dylan to confirm provisioning schedule and post-provision smoke tests
- Evelyn to own rollback criteria and runbook publication

I'll be the primary customer contact during the window and will join the incident channel. Marking this thread as approved — please move the routing plan to the ops runbook and post the HubSpot deal update once provisioning is scheduled.

— Soojin Lee
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
